notes: Examined `function checkpoint() public`, which writes state, carries no modifier and never mentions msg.sender -- which is what the predicate reports. It is permissionless by design and there is nothing for a caller to direct: the function takes no parameters, every destination it pays (`treasury`, each token's configured adapter) is read from state, and the body is gated by `if (block.timestamp >= currentEpoch + WEEK)` so it advances at most once per epoch. The only thing a caller chooses is when to trigger work the contract would do anyway, bounded by that epoch check. Not an instance of access_control at this location. This says nothing about the rest of the file.
